Experiment 9: Orthogonal vs Destructive Prompts — llama3.1:8b

10 questions × 5 conditions × 300 completions. Tests whether geometrically orthogonal prompts outperform both standard and deliberately destructive prompts.

Prompt Sentence Embedding UMAP

System prompt sentences (red) should cluster separately from orthogonal (green). Destructive (black) may overlap with system. Exp1 (blue) and random (gray) fall between.

Interference Correlation

Each dot = one prompt sentence. X = max similarity to system prompt, Y = spread delta (positive = more spread than unconstrained, negative = tighter). If correlation holds, prompt-space similarity predicts output-space interference.

Regression: slope=-0.1105, intercept=0.1277, R²=0.020

If R² > 0.3, prompt-space similarity to the system prompt predicts output-space interference.

Average Efficiency Frontier

Shaded area = interference cost. Green = orthogonal (spread should decrease). Red = destructive (spread should increase).
